A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TF/ETF trust-discounting research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, agreement, uncertainty, noise-robustness, and warm-up experiments on six datasets, including results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original Food101 experiments, component and sensitivity ablations, feature-similarity analyses, and comparative timing measurements.

M1.justification: The documented warm-up target changes from eta*z + eta/2 in v1 Section 2.3 to eta*z + (1-eta)/2 in v2 Section 3.3, correcting the target used in the loss. The referral architecture, discounting rule, fusion, and four-stage training procedure otherwise remain intact. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: v2 retains all six original datasets and adds Food101 image-text food classification in Section 4.4. This substantially extends coverage beyond the original feature-vector benchmarks to evaluation with image and text encoders trained end to end.

E2.justification: TMNR and CCML are added to the six-dataset accuracy, Kappa, MVAGT, and AUROC comparisons. F-Mode and F-Avg disappear from the accuracy, Kappa, and MVAGT tables, although they participate in v2's expanded timing comparisons. These are substantive changes in comparator membership.

E3.justification: The new Food101 protocol uses pretrained ResNet50 and base-uncased BERT, AdamW fine-tuning, and 61,127/6,845/22,716 training/validation/test instances. New ablations control TD participation, smoothing factors, and view combinations. The original six-dataset 80/20 splits and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 Section 4.3 adds tests isolating the TD module, sensitivity to label smoothing, and the contribution of different Scene15 views. Appendix D.4 adds pairwise feature-similarity analysis, and Appendix E.2 expands efficiency analysis. The earlier warm-up study, noise tests, conflict heatmaps, and CUB case study are retained.

E5.justification: The original predictive metrics retain ten seeded runs with mean and standard deviation. Food101 specifies three runs with mean and standard deviation. Timing tables change from single-run values to ten-run averages with ± values; v1 already mentioned ten repetitions, so this establishes changed reporting rather than an increase in runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds comparator, Food101, ablation, similarity, and comparative timing results while removing F-Mode/F-Avg predictive rows. Food101 reports ETF accuracy of 93.09±0.02. Matching original predictive rows are otherwise unchanged except TMC's CUB AUROC, which changes from 64.80±10.5 in v1 Table 5 to 63.80±10.5 in v2 Table 13. Timing values are replaced under changed reporting, not evidence of a same-setting speedup.

T1.justification: v2 broadens the conflict definition beyond confident opposing predictions, revises the first proposition's proof to invoke training objectives, and adds a bilinear-layer time-complexity derivation in Appendix E.2. Both central propositions and the existing fusion and evidence-update derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: learnable instance-wise trust discounting, stage-wise training, and improved classification accuracy and cross-view agreement. The additional experiments support these existing contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 newly explains agreement improvements through training-time gradient interactions, relates feature similarity to conflict patterns, and proposes insufficient training data as an additional explanation for AUROC degradation. It also acknowledges stage-wise training cost as a limitation. The earlier warm-up-loss limitation and corrected-but-uncertain CUB explanation remain.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands documentation with feature descriptions and extractors, exact split counts, Adam defaults, Food101 encoder settings, and Python/CUDA/OS versions. Runtime documentation is also expanded. However, v1's explicit Gaussian-noise recipe affecting randomly selected half-views is omitted. Both versions still promise code release upon acceptance.

R1.justification: v2 adds TMNR, CCML, and feature-extractor references, removes the GAN training-inspiration and medical-example references, and clarifies instance-wise discounting relative to prior global trust discounting. Its main positioning within subjective logic and evidential multi-view classification remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the motivation and method explanations, replaces the medical example with navigation, moves related work before the method, and reorganizes the appendices. MVAGT, AUROC, and noise results move out of the main text; a simplified main algorithm accompanies detailed appendix algorithms. Terminology and authorship also change.

P2.justification: v2 converts the main text to two columns, replaces Figure 1, redraws Figure 2, and replaces the original fusion illustration with three worked-example tables. It adds ablation, Food101, similarity, and expanded timing tables. Existing empirical plots are retained and redistributed, with revised captions rather than new plotted results.

improvement.justification: The new component ablations and Food101 evaluation improve assessment of the method's contribution and applicability, while expanded implementation and timing disclosures improve transparency. These gains outweigh, but are moderated by, removing useful predictive baselines—including F-Avg, which led Caltech101 accuracy in v1—and omitting the earlier noise-generation protocol.
